verses.text: In the third year that Hoshea son of Elah was king of Israel, Hezekiah son of Ahaz began to rule as king of Judah.
He was twenty-five years old when he became king, and he ruled in Jerusalem for twenty-nine years. His mother was Abi, the daughter of Zechariah.
He did what was right in the LORD's eyes, just as his ancestor David had done.

He removed the high places, smashed the sacred stone pillars, and cut down the Asherah poles. He also broke into pieces the bronze snake Moses had made, because up to that time the Israelites had been burning incense to it. It was called Nehushtan.
Hezekiah trusted in the LORD, the God of Israel. There was no one like him among all the kings of Judah, either before him or after him.
He held tight to the LORD and never stopped following him. He kept the commands the LORD had given Moses.
The LORD was with him, and he was successful in everything he did. He rebelled against the king of Assyria and refused to serve him.
He defeated the Philistines as far as Gaza and its territory, from the smallest watchtower to the biggest walled city.
In the fourth year of King Hezekiah, which was the seventh year that Hoshea son of Elah was king of Israel, Shalmaneser king of Assyria attacked Samaria and surrounded it.
At the end of three years the Assyrians captured it. So Samaria was captured in the sixth year of Hezekiah, which was the ninth year that Hoshea was king of Israel.
The king of Assyria took the Israelites away to Assyria and settled them in Halah, at the Habor River in Gozan, and in the towns of the Medes.
This happened because they had not obeyed the LORD their God. They had broken his covenant and everything Moses the LORD's servant had commanded. They would not listen, and they would not obey.
In the fourteenth year of King Hezekiah, Sennacherib king of Assyria attacked all the walled cities of Judah and captured them.

So Hezekiah king of Judah sent this message to the king of Assyria at Lachish: "I have done wrong. Leave me alone, and I will pay whatever you demand." The king of Assyria demanded that Hezekiah king of Judah pay about ten thousand kilograms of silver and about one thousand kilograms of gold.
So Hezekiah gave him all the silver found in the LORD's temple and in the treasuries of the palace.
At that time Hezekiah also stripped the gold from the doors and doorposts of the LORD's temple, gold he himself had put there, and gave it to the king of Assyria.

The king of Assyria sent his supreme commander, his chief officer, and his field commander from Lachish to King Hezekiah in Jerusalem, with a large army. They came up to Jerusalem and stopped by the water channel of the Upper Pool, on the road to the Washerman's Field.
They called for the king. Eliakim son of Hilkiah, who was in charge of the palace, Shebna the secretary, and Joah son of Asaph, the record keeper, went out to meet them.
The field commander said to them, "Tell Hezekiah, 'This is what the great king, the king of Assyria, says: What are you trusting in?
You say you have a plan and the strength for war, but those are just empty words. Who are you trusting in, that you have rebelled against me?
Look, you are trusting in Egypt, that broken reed of a walking stick! If a man leans on it, it will stab into his hand. That is what Pharaoh king of Egypt is like to everyone who trusts in him.

But perhaps you will tell me, "We are trusting in the LORD our God." Isn't he the one whose high places and altars Hezekiah removed? Didn't Hezekiah tell Judah and Jerusalem, "You must worship only at this altar in Jerusalem"?
Now then, make a deal with my master, the king of Assyria. I will give you two thousand horses, if you can find enough riders to put on them!
How can you push back even the weakest officer among my master's servants? Yet you trust in Egypt for chariots and horsemen!
Besides, have I come to attack and destroy this place without the LORD? The LORD himself told me, "Go up against this land and destroy it."'"

Then Eliakim son of Hilkiah, Shebna, and Joah said to the field commander, "Please speak to your servants in Aramaic, because we understand it. Do not speak to us in Hebrew where the people on the wall can hear."

But the field commander answered, "Did my master send me to say these things only to your master and to you? No, he sent me to the men sitting on the wall too. Like you, they will soon have to eat their own dung and drink their own urine."
Then the field commander stood and shouted in Hebrew, "Listen to the word of the great king, the king of Assyria!
This is what the king says: 'Do not let Hezekiah fool you. He cannot rescue you from my power.
Do not let Hezekiah get you to trust in the LORD by saying, "The LORD will surely rescue us. This city will not be handed over to the king of Assyria."

Do not listen to Hezekiah.' This is what the king of Assyria says: 'Make peace with me and come out to me. Then each of you will eat from your own vine and your own fig tree, and drink water from your own well,

until I come and take you to a land like your own. It is a land of grain and new wine, a land of bread and vineyards, a land of olive trees and honey. Choose life and not death! Do not listen to Hezekiah when he misleads you by saying, "The LORD will rescue us."
Has the god of any nation ever rescued his land from the power of the king of Assyria?
Where are the gods of Hamath and Arpad? Where are the gods of Sepharvaim, Hena, and Ivvah? Did they rescue Samaria from my power?
Which of all the gods of these countries has been able to save his land from me? So how could the LORD save Jerusalem from me?'"
But the people kept quiet and did not say a word in reply, because the king had commanded, "Do not answer him."

Then Eliakim son of Hilkiah, who was in charge of the palace, Shebna the secretary, and Joah son of Asaph, the record keeper, went to Hezekiah with their clothes torn, and told him what the field commander had said.
